fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar advanced to 0.7305 USD (USD/CAD ~1.369), gaining +1.5% over the period as WTI's rebound from its April 17 trough supported the commodity-linked currency.1 Forecasters project USD/CAD in the 1.37-1.40 range near-term, with potential strengthening toward 1.34 by year-end if BoC tightening materializes.2 The Canada-U.S. rate differential narrowed as bond markets priced ~41 basis points of BoC tightening by December, while the Fed is expected to hold at 3.50%-3.75%.3 The euro gained on ECB hawkish signaling, while the yen strengthened on safe-haven demand. The yuan remained stable as China's +5.0% Q1 GDP print exceeded the 4.8% consensus — relevant for Canada's 305 mining projects ($146.0B) with exposure to Chinese commodity demand.4

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve steepened at the front end while bear-flattening at longer tenors. The 2-year yield rose 35 basis points as markets repriced BoC rate expectations from cuts to potential tightening.5 The 5-year benchmark — the reference rate for most fixed-rate mortgages and project financing — stood at 3.06%, down 0.13 percentage points over the past month but up 0.26 percentage points year-over-year.5 The 10-year traded at approximately 3.48%. Bond market pricing implies a ~92% probability of hold at the April 29 decision, with tightening expected later in 2026.6 The 10-year/2-year spread of 56 basis points reflects market expectations for higher near-term policy rates relative to long-run neutral, signaling a normalization cycle rather than recessionary inversion.5
